text: The book classifies Laplace's equation ∇²u = 0 as a hyperbolic PDE whose natural well-posed problem is the specification of Cauchy (initial) data.
explanation: False on both counts: Laplace's equation has B² − AC < 0, so it is elliptic, not hyperbolic. Its well-posed formulation is a boundary value problem (Dirichlet or Neumann); imposing Cauchy data on an elliptic equation is Hadamard's classic ill-posed example, where high-frequency perturbations blow up.
